clue.text: Artillery officer's foolish raid in Wellington, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the aircraft's name

parts.note: the Vickers Wellington was a Second World War bomber, hence 'perhaps'

indicators.note: foolish suggests the letters of raid are scrambled senselessly

explanation.surface: An army officer leads a silly raid somewhere in New Zealand's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' looks like the city or the Duke, but it is the wartime aircraft. 'foolish' turns RAID into ARDI, which goes 'in' BOMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardier is a non-commissioned rank in the British artillery, roughly equal to a corporal.

clue.text: British Unionist member's minor collision

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for Unionist, as in Ulster parties
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A political figure from Northern Ireland has a small car accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is a light knock or slight crash between vehicles.

clue.text: Doctor against breaking links gives reasons

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor

indicators.note: breaking means the short word splits the links apart and sits within them

parts.note: ties are links or connections
V for versus, against

explanation.surface: A physician opposed to severing connections explains why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' gives V, from versus, as in sports fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: Motives are the grounds or causes that drive someone to act.

clue.text: Slow-to-be-expressed ideas, but time during pudding

indicators.note: during says the conjunction and time letter come within the dessert word

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding, the dessert course
though can mean but, as in 'it rained, though not much'

explanation.surface: Ideas come late, but only while dessert is being eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British informal for the pudding or dessert course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions that occur later, after the main decision, are late-arriving ideas.

clue.text: Took off in feat crossing channel

indicators.note: crossing means the achievement word straddles the passage word, holding it

parts.note: a deed is a feat or exploit
a duct is a channel or tube

explanation.surface: Someone flew off during a heroic achievement such as crossing the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off an amount is to subtract it, as from a bill.

clue.text: Figures from folklore, topless personalities

indicators.note: topless says the first letter of the word is removed, the top of a down entry

parts.note: selves are personalities or identities

explanation.surface: Mythical characters turn out to be people without clothes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small magical beings found in European legend and tales.

clue.text: Napoleon's campaign must reveal this dirty trick

indicators.note: must reveal says the letters lie in plain view across the two words

explanation.surface: The French emperor's military campaign will expose a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Napoleon's' into 'campaign'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle or deceptive scheme to cheat people.

clue.text: Commit prisoner on notice

parts.note: con is slang for convict, a prisoner
a sign is a notice put up for people to read

explanation.surface: A convict is sent to jail by a posted order.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign is to hand over or commit something to another's care or a place.

clue.text: Examines financial status of tight-fisted international on board

parts.note: mean means stingy or tight-fisted

indicators.note: on board conventionally means put inside SS, the steamship letters

parts.note: board here stands for a ship, SS, which one goes on board
a test is an international match, as in Test cricket

explanation.surface: A stingy foreign player on a committee checks people's wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention of putting something inside SS (steamship). A Test is an international cricket or rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessments of income used to decide eligibility for benefits are checks of financial standing.

clue.text: Took another form, subdued about a source of tension,

indicators.note: about means the quiet word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: muted means subdued or toned down

indicators.note: source of picks the opening letter, where the word begins

explanation.surface: Something changed shape, quietened around the origin of stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to change in form or nature, like a gene altering.

clue.text: Terrace of museum visited by the Queen

indicators.note: visited by says the royal letters come into the museum's name

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A museum's outdoor area receives a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed platform along a house, much like a terrace.

clue.text: Rebel, accepting gradual development, to make great changes

indicators.note: accepting means the verb takes the long noun into itself

parts.note: to rise, or rise up, is to rebel
evolution is gradual development over time

explanation.surface: An insurgent agrees to slow progress in order to transform things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebel' looks like a noun but is the verb RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolutionise something is to transform it radically.

clue.text: Recreated Versace vision, seeing these on pins

indicators.note: recreated means the letters are made over in a new order

explanation.surface: A revived designer's collection is seen on someone's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen, twisted blood vessels commonly appear on the legs, called pins informally.

clue.text: Electronic devices that could make armies flip

indicators.note: could make says the letters given can be rearranged to form the result

explanation.surface: Gadgets capable of making whole armies turn somersaults.
explanation.definitionFit: Amplifiers are circuits that boost the strength of a signal, as in sound systems.

clue.text: Jiggery-pokery evidenced by Military Intelligence's boss

parts.note: MI is Military Intelligence, with the possessive S kept
a chief is a boss or leader

explanation.surface: Underhand dealings are shown by the head of the spy service.
explanation.definitionFit: Jiggery-pokery is underhand trickery or naughtiness, which is what mischief is.

clue.text: Dive exercises incorporating breather

indicators.note: incorporating means the short abbreviation takes the organ word inside

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises
a lung is what one breathes with

explanation.surface: Swimming drills include a moment of rest before the dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' suggests a rest, but it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to dive or jump headlong into water.

clue.text: Agents repeatedly strike loudly for bread

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, its agents

indicators.note: loudly says we take what the words sound like when spoken

parts.note: to batter is to strike over and over

explanation.surface: Spies keep beating something noisily in pursuit of a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciabatta is a flat, open-textured Italian white loaf.

clue.text: Primate's indolence, dismissing nothing

indicators.note: dismissing means the round zero letter is sent away from the word

parts.note: languor is lazy listlessness, indolence
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A monkey's laziness leads it to reject everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A langur is a long-tailed Asian monkey, so a kind of primate.

clue.text: Essential massage is said to precede outbreak of flu

indicators.note: is said tells us to take how the word for massaging sounds when spoken

parts.note: to knead is to massage with the hands

indicators.note: outbreak of suggests the letters of the illness breaking out into new order

explanation.surface: A rubdown is said to be vital before the flu season arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful means necessary, required, indispensable.

clue.text: Detective's characteristic — thinking of other things

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, with the possessive S
a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: An investigator's typical quality is a wandering mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrait means absent-minded or distracted, with attention elsewhere.

clue.text: Notice study with Russian's affirmative supplementary notes

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
a den is a study, a private room
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: Someone notices a study whose Russian yes adds footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added at the end of a book, extra material.

clue.text: Items anathema to a vegetarian family

definitions.meaning: meat and blood are what a vegetarian refuses

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means one's own relatives, and literally meat and blood avoided by non-meat-eaters.

clue.text: Closed union is set up to expose such models

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
to expose says the letters are laid bare inside the two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A closed shop union is formed to reveal unclothed artists' models.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left the hidden word without its signal: 'to expose' reveals the letters, so the definition is just 'such models', with 'set up' reading them upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Life models who pose unclothed for artists are posing in the bare, as figure studies.

clue.text: Poems soldiers regularly used

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, the even ones here

explanation.surface: Verses that troops regularly recited.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems usually addressed to a subject.

clue.text: Gushed, seeing energy employed by two females

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
F is female, so two give FF
used means employed

explanation.surface: A pair of women enthused after being given jobs and drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To effuse is to pour out or flow forth, so to gush.

clue.text: Canned outside hotel and diluted

indicators.note: outside means the preserved-food word wraps around the letter

parts.note: tinned means canned
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone was fired outside a hotel and watered down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' suggests sacked, but it means preserved in tins.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinned liquid has been made weaker or less concentrated.

clue.text: Only fools ultimately cheer in Spain

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter, at the very end

parts.note: ole is the Spanish shout of approval

explanation.surface: Only idiots end up shouting at bullfights in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single or only, as in sole survivor.

clue.text: Land Rovers?

parts.note: an estate is a tract of land
cars rove the roads; Land Rover is also a car make

explanation.surface: A question about the off-road vehicle brand.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the brand name Land Rover is being split into two ordinary words.
explanation.definitionFit: Some Land Rover models are station wagons, vehicles with a long rear load area.
